samples.question: The gray line in this picture is one single continuous cord. It never branches, never touches itself and has exactly two loose ends. Three round beads - one red, one blue and one amber - are threaded on that cord at three different places along it. Walk along the cord itself from one loose end to the other, following every bend, and note the order in which you pass the three beads. Exactly one bead is passed second, that is, it lies between the other two beads along the cord; this middle bead is the same whichever end you start from. Straight-line distance across the picture does not matter, and a bead that looks like it sits between the other two in the picture need not be the middle one along the cord. Which bead is the middle one along the cord? Answer red, blue, or amber.
